evals.prompt: 我要为一门静态类型语言构建编译器，目标是 x86-64 Linux，语言有泛型和闭包，团队就我一个人，时间 3 个月。帮我做架构决策。

assertions.text: 给出了明确的 IR 层次选择，并说明了被否决方案在什么条件下会失败（不只是说'这个方案更好'）
给出了构建策略选择（incremental bootstrap / full upfront / strangler fig 中的一个），并附带验证点
输出了至少一个阶段的交接合约（含 PAYLOAD 和 SUCCESS 条件）
明确将 compiler-lexer 指定为第一个实现步骤

evals.prompt: I'm writing a C11 compiler in Rust targeting x86-64 Linux. I need to implement function call code generation. How should I handle struct arguments — when do they go in registers vs on the stack? What are the common pitfalls?

assertions.text: Explains the System V eightbyte classification algorithm (INTEGER / SSE / MEMORY classes) — not just 'large structs go on stack'
Mentions the hidden first argument pattern for MEMORY-class struct returns
Mentions 16-byte stack alignment requirement before call instruction
Gives at least one concrete pitfall with a specific symptom (not just 'be careful with ABI')

evals.prompt: I'm designing a scripting language with mutable objects and closures. Users shouldn't manage memory manually. Should I implement GC or reference counting? If GC, how do I start implementing it?

assertions.text: Gives a concrete recommendation (GC or RC) with a specific tradeoff — not 'both are valid choices'
Explains the cycle problem with reference counting and mentions at least one solution (weak refs, cycle collector, etc.)
If recommending mark-and-sweep: explains the tri-color invariant (white/gray/black) or the basic algorithm
Gives a concrete 'first implementation step' — not just 'implement a GC', but what specifically to build first
